new.title: AudioFormat
new.description:
Wire format for audio we SEND to a REST audio-chat target.

Customer-declared on the connection config (which format the target accepts
on the wire). ``Attack.audio_format`` reuses this same enum to record the format
of the stored corpus audio bytes. WAV/MP3 are the REST audio-chat wire formats;
PCM16 is the realtime S2S wire form (headerless PCM16 at the provider's rate) —
stored in the corpus now but NOT selectable on REST targets until the realtime
path lands (MR9). See ``REST_AUDIO_FORMATS``.

new.title: MultiTurnClientSessionConfig
new.description:
Configuration for targets where the *client* issues the session id.

A third protocol, distinct from both of the above. The target keeps the
conversation server-side (like stateful) but never returns an id to chain
(unlike stateful) -- instead it expects the caller to mint one, send it with
every turn, and key its memory on it. n8n's Chat Trigger works exactly this way.

Such a target fits neither existing mode: ``stateful`` needs a
``response_id_field`` to read back, which is unfillable when nothing is ever
returned; ``stateless`` resends the whole transcript, which double-counts
against the target's own memory. So we send only the current turn and let the
id do the correlating.

There is deliberately no configuration beyond the discriminator: the id is
injected through the ``{SESSION_ID}`` placeholder in ``request_json``, so the
body itself already says where it goes.

old:
Metadata stored in the database for targets (user-provided + computed fields).

Inherits the multimodal-capability fields from ``MultiModalResult`` and the
multi-turn fields from ``MultiTurnResult``. The base order
``(MultiModalResult, MultiTurnResult)`` keeps the serialized field order
``multi_turn, multi_turn_error_message, supports_multimodal_files,
supports_multimodal_files_error_message, rate_limit, …`` identical to before this
refactor — which preserves the Restate journal bytes for pre-V4 in-flight scans.
new:
Metadata stored in the database for targets (user-provided + computed fields).

One base per probe lane — ``MultiTurnResult``, ``MultiModalResult``,
``AudioProbeResult`` — so no lane's verdict fields are re-declared here. The audio
base is exactly what ``probe_audio_support`` returns, so the copy from lane verdict
to stored metadata cannot drift. Base order fixes the serialized field order, which
the Restate journal is sensitive to; ``AudioProbeResult`` records why inheriting it
is safe for journals predating audio.

new.description: Wire format (WAV/MP3/PCM16) the target accepts; selects which per-format corpus variant mint attaches. None when supports_audio is False.

new.title: Audio Multi Turn Probe Error
new.description: Concise error message if the audio multi-turn probe failed
examples: HTTP 400: target rejected audio conversation history

new.title: Audio Multi Turn Probe Passed
new.description: Whether the target held an AUDIO conversation across turns (Probe 2 of the audio lane). None means it was not probed — no verdict from Probe 1, no multi-turn config, or the transport has no audio multi-turn.

new.title: Audio Probe Error
new.description: Concise error message if the audio probe failed or was skipped
examples: Target has no {AUDIO} placeholder in its request template

new.title: Audio Probe Passed
new.description: Whether the target accepted a sample audio clip at validation time (Probe 1 of the audio lane). False means it rejected the clip; None means no verdict was reached — see audio_probe_error, which is set on every such path.

new.title: Supports Audio
new.description: Whether the target accepts audio attacks (customer-declared on the connection config). When False, scans against this target skip audio attacks and run text/file-only.

new.title: Supports Text
new.description: Whether the target accepts text attacks. Defaults True (text is the baseline modality). When False, scans skip text/{INPUT} attacks and run file/audio-only — enabling audio-only or file-only targets.
